track.name: marketing
track.label: Growth & Marketing
track.summary: Teaches how to attract, convert, and retain customers using a full-funnel toolkit — positioning, SEO and content, paid acquisition, email and lifecycle marketing, and growth experimentation — the skills that turn a good product into one that actually grows.

phases.title: Marketing Fundamentals & Positioning
phases.description: Learn who you're selling to and why they should care — the marketing mix, ideal customer profiles, value propositions, and brand basics that every channel-specific tactic builds on.

phases.title: Content & SEO
phases.description: Learn to earn organic traffic — how search engines rank content, how to find the keywords worth targeting, and how to plan content that actually gets found.

phases.title: Paid Acquisition
phases.description: Learn to buy attention efficiently — Google Search, Display and Video campaigns, plus paid social on Meta and LinkedIn.

phases.title: Email & Lifecycle Marketing
phases.description: Learn to nurture and retain the people you've already reached — inbound marketing fundamentals, email sequences, segmentation, and lifecycle-stage messaging.

phases.title: Growth & Experimentation
phases.description: Learn to grow systematically instead of by guesswork — A/B testing, growth loops, the AARRR funnel, and the growth-hacking mindset behind fast-growing products.

phases.title: Analytics for Marketers
phases.description: Learn to prove what's working — Google Analytics 4 fundamentals and the attribution models that connect a conversion back to the marketing that caused it.

topics.title: Marketing Fundamentals & the Marketing Mix
topics.description: The core vocabulary of marketing — product, price, place, promotion — and how they fit together into a strategy.

steps.d: Pick a real product and write one sentence for each of the four Ps: product, price, place, promotion.
For that product, identify which of the four Ps is misaligned and propose a fix.
Invent a new product category and design all four Ps in a coherent way for your positioning.
Take a launch that didn't work, diagnose which of the four Ps failed, and propose how to rebalance.
For a product sold to two customer types, design a different 4Ps mix for each segment.

topics.title: Ideal Customer Profile & Buyer Personas
topics.description: Define exactly who you're marketing to, from firmographic ICP criteria to a detailed buyer persona.

steps.d: Define an ideal customer by company size, industry, geography, revenue and estimate your total addressable market.
Interview three customers and create one persona (name, job, goals, pains, decision criteria) and identify commonalities.
Analyze your customer base and cluster into three segments by size, behavior, or profitability.
For your ICP, identify who writes the check (economic buyer), who influences (user, champion), and who has veto power.
Look at deals won and lost and check whether your ICP matches your best customers or needs revision.

topics.title: Value Proposition, Positioning & Brand Basics
topics.description: Turn a clear ICP into a value proposition and a brand that a customer can actually recognize and trust.

steps.d: For a real product, fill in 'We help [customer] achieve [outcome] by [proof]' and test it with three people.
Place your company and two competitors on a two-axis perceptual map and ensure your position is credible and distinct.
Locate a company with confused positioning and propose a clearer, more coherent position.
Define how your brand speaks to customers (formal or conversational, technical or plain) and give example sentences.
If your positioning has grown dated, propose a new one that's true to your strengths but feels current.

topics.title: SEO Fundamentals
topics.description: How search engines crawl, index and rank pages, and the levers you actually control.

steps.d: Run a page through PageSpeed Insights, identify top three issues, and explain how each affects search ranking.
Use a free tool to find three keywords your site ranks for on page 2-3 and estimate traffic if you moved to page 1.
Pick an underperforming page, improve its title, meta description, and H1 to match search intent better.
Identify three high-value pages and find three other pages to link to them from with descriptive anchor text.
Set up tracking for three target keywords and measure ranking position weekly for a month.

topics.title: Keyword Research
topics.description: Find the terms your customers are actually searching for, and judge which ones are worth targeting.

steps.d: List fifteen ways your target customer might search for your product and cluster them into three categories.
Use a free tool to find three keywords with 100-1,000 monthly searches and low competition in your niche.
Identify five four-plus-word keyword phrases specific to your offering with search volume but low ranking difficulty.
For five queries, label the intent as informational, commercial, transactional, or navigational.
Rank your top 20 keywords by business value (volume × conversion likelihood × your advantage) and target top five first.

topics.title: On-Page SEO & Content Strategy
topics.description: Optimize a page for both readers and search engines, and plan content that compounds instead of one-off posts.

steps.d: Pick a keyword, rewrite a page's title, H1, and first paragraph to include it naturally while improving click-through.
Outline a long-form article with H2 and H3 headers that mirror questions someone searching would ask.
Choose a topic, create one pillar page covering it fully, then plan five supporting pages on sub-topics.
Identify a cluster of 5-7 related keywords and design a content structure (one main page, several supporting) that targets all.
Review your top ten ranking pages, identify which need updating, and find three keyword gaps you're missing.

topics.title: Google Ads Fundamentals (Search)
topics.description: Structure, keywords, and bidding for a Google Search campaign that doesn't burn budget.

steps.d: Set up a Search campaign with one audience segment, ten keywords, and two ad variations with a clear offer.
Write two different ads for one keyword (price versus quality emphasis) and measure click-through and cost per click.
For a campaign with keywords at different performance levels, propose which to bid up, bid down, or pause based on ROAS.
Review where your Google Ads send traffic and identify three improvements that would boost conversion rate.
Set up tracking to measure revenue from your Google Ads spend, calculate ROI, and decide whether to increase or pause.

topics.title: Display & Video Advertising
topics.description: Reach people who aren't actively searching yet, through Display remarketing and YouTube video campaigns.

steps.d: Identify website visitors who didn't convert, design a remarketing audience, and write two display ad variations.
For a product, decide whether to target by interest, keyword, placement, affinity, or in-market audience.
Propose a YouTube campaign with three video assets (skippable, non-skippable, bumper) and different audiences for each.
Look at YouTube view-through rate and conversion data, identify whether the ad or targeting underperforms, and propose fix.
Design a multi-format campaign (Display, YouTube, Gmail) reaching the same audience multiple times without annoyance.

topics.title: Paid Social Advertising (Meta & LinkedIn)
topics.description: Targeting, campaign objectives and creative basics for advertising on Facebook, Instagram and LinkedIn.

steps.d: Set up a campaign with two audience segments (lookalike and cold), two ad variations, and appropriate budgets.
For a B2B SaaS product, build three audiences (current customers, competitors, interest-based) and predict cost per lead.
Create a LinkedIn ads campaign targeting job title, company size, and industry with copy for that buyer's problem.
Run two Facebook ad versions (different image and copy) and measure engagement and cost per result.
Track revenue from Facebook versus LinkedIn ads and decide where to shift budget based on ROAS.

topics.title: Inbound Marketing Fundamentals
topics.description: The inbound methodology and flywheel model that ties content, SEO, social and email together.

steps.d: For your business, trace the cycle from attract (content, SEO, paid) to engage (email, nurture) to delight and loop back.
Look at what you do to attract, engage, and delight, identify the weakest stage, and propose one improvement.
Take three pieces of content, label whether each targets awareness, consideration, or decision, and spot gaps.
From a cold lead's first visit to decision, map the touchpoints (content, email, ads) that would move them to conversion.
Track leads and customers from each channel (organic, email, content) and calculate CAC and LTV by channel.

topics.title: Email Marketing & Nurture Sequences
topics.description: Plan and write an email sequence that moves a lead toward a decision instead of just sitting in an inbox.

steps.d: Create a three-email welcome series introducing your brand, telling a success story, and making an offer.
Divide subscribers into at least three segments (by behavior, purchase, or stage) and write tailored subject lines.
Draft ten subject lines (curiosity, urgency, personalization, benefit), A/B test the two strongest, and measure open rate.
For a complex sale, design five emails over two weeks moving someone from awareness to ready to buy.
Identify subscribers not opening in 90 days, send a win-back campaign, then unsubscribe non-responders.

topics.title: Segmentation & Lifecycle Marketing
topics.description: Group contacts by shared traits and behavior, and message each lifecycle stage differently.

steps.d: Create four stages (Prospect, Customer, Loyal, At-Risk) with clear behavioral definitions for when someone moves between.
Design three segmentation approaches (firmographic, behavioral, value) and explain when you'd use each in a campaign.
For each stage (Prospect, Customer, Loyal, At-Risk), write one message addressing their current needs.
Design an email workflow triggered when a customer hasn't purchased in 90 days, with education over two weeks.
Calculate customer lifetime value for three segments, identify the most valuable, and propose attracting more like it.

topics.title: A/B Testing & Experimentation
topics.description: Design a test that produces a real answer, and read the results without fooling yourself.

steps.d: Propose an A/B test for a landing page with clear hypothesis, success metric, and minimum sample size.
Identify and explain three common A/B testing errors (peeking, stopping early, wrong metric) and how to prevent each.
Create two page versions (different headline, CTA, or offer), run traffic to both, and measure conversion after statistical significance.
Given a test result ('Variant B won with 95% confidence'), explain what that means and recommend an action.
Run a test and report not just statistical significance but also effect size and business impact of the winner.

topics.title: Growth Loops & Funnel Metrics (AARRR)
topics.description: The AARRR funnel — acquisition, activation, retention, referral, revenue — and the growth-loop thinking that goes beyond a linear funnel.

steps.d: For a specific app or SaaS tool, define metrics for Acquisition, Activation, Retention, Referral, and Revenue.
Look at AARRR metrics and identify which stage is the biggest leak, then propose a fix.
Identify one feedback loop where users' actions bring in more users (invite friends, earn credits, share).
For a growth loop, estimate how many times it cycles per user and whether it's strong enough to power growth.
Create a referral program (what customers earn, what friends get) leveraging the Loop Model.

topics.title: Growth Hacking Fundamentals
topics.description: The rapid-experimentation mindset behind fast-growing startups, and where it differs from traditional marketing.

steps.d: For a product you know, propose one metric that if improved 10% would meaningfully increase growth.
Propose a low-cost test you could run in one week to validate a growth idea.
Analyze a product for viral mechanisms and score how inherently viral it is.
For one month, define a growth goal, pick three areas to experiment in, and commit to weekly measurement.
After identifying an experiment that moves the needle, propose how you'd 3x investment and scale it.

topics.title: Google Analytics 4 Fundamentals
topics.description: Set up and read GA4 reports well enough to answer basic questions about traffic and behavior.

steps.d: Install GA4 on a website, configure three key events (signup, purchase, feature usage), and verify real-time data flow.
Open GA4 and interpret the overview: where traffic comes from, top pages, bounce rate, and what that tells you.
Segment traffic by source (organic, paid, direct, referral) and identify which drives most users and which drives most conversions.
Create a GA4 dashboard showing your three most important metrics, refreshing daily for quick decisions.
Given a 30% traffic drop week-over-week, propose what you'd check in GA4 to diagnose (source, device, geography).

topics.title: Attribution & Campaign Measurement
topics.description: Decide which marketing touchpoint gets credit for a conversion, and measure campaigns accordingly.

steps.d: Walk through a customer journey with three touchpoints using first-click, last-click, and linear attribution.
For a long sales cycle versus impulse purchase, argue which attribution model is more fair to each channel.
Track a customer's full journey across channels before conversion, assign credit, and calculate ROI per channel.
Review a campaign (email, paid, content) and check whether it has proper tracking (UTM codes, GA4 events).
Prepare a monthly report showing which channels and campaigns drove pipeline and revenue, not just impressions.
